brique._comment: Engine-native control-channel capacity. Not dispatched by ReflexiveLoop family routing — routed directly to the addressed context's control channel (to.type="control") and handled by ContextLoop.run/StartChildren.

objective.name: context.start
objective.description: Load and start one or more child contexts that exist on disk but are not yet running in memory.

#root.role: For each named child, validate it is not already loaded, confirm a context.json exists for it on disk, create its ContextLoop, and install it under the addressed parent context. Emit one response with a per-child result.

child._comment: Required. Name of the direct child context to start, or an array of such names (single path segments, as created by edit.create with type "context"). Blank array entries are dropped.

result._comment: One entry per requested child, in request order: { child (string), ok (bool), reason (string, present only when ok is false) }.

effects.context_tree: A new ContextLoop is created and installed in memory for each successfully started child. No files are written — each child's context.json must already exist on disk (typically created beforehand via edit.create with type "context").

transformation_contract.morphing: A start request for one or more on-disk-but-unloaded child contexts becomes a running ContextLoop for each child that could be started, with a per-child outcome reported back to the caller.
invariants: Each requested child must be a direct child name of the addressed context (single path segment).
The addressed (parent) context must itself be running.
A child must not already be loaded in memory — use context.restart for an already-running child; such a child is reported with ok=false and an explanatory reason.
A context.json must already exist on disk at <parent_dir>/<child> for each requested child — context.start never creates it. Use edit.create with type "context" first.
Children are processed sequentially and independently — one child's failure does not prevent the others from being attempted.
success: response.status is "ok" only when every requested child started successfully.
payload.result always lists one entry per requested child, in request order, whether the overall response is ok or error.
failure: response.status is "error" (code: refused) when params.child is valid but at least one requested child failed to start; response.error.details.result carries the same per-child breakdown as the ok payload.
response.status is "error" (code: invalid) when params.child is missing, empty, or neither a string nor an array of strings — no child is attempted in this case.
notes: This is the cold-start path for a child context created after its parent already started — createChildrenFromDescriptor only loads children_list entries at parent startup time.
Typical sequence: edit.create (type: context) to materialize the child on disk, then context.start with params.child set to the same name (or a list of names) to bring it to life.
Always inspect payload.result (or response.error.details.result) rather than assuming response.status alone tells you which children started.
